Drop all observations with missing values, if there is still any, from the “NHL_Game” dataframe.


Show code
NHL_game = NHL_game.dropna()


Create two dataframes that separate the “NHL_Game” dataframe by home and away games. Name them “NHL_Home” and “NHL_Away”, respectively.

Rename variables:

For away games, rename “ascore” to “goals_for”; rename “hscore” to “goals_against”
For home games, rename “hscore” to “goals_for”; rename “ascore” to “goals_against”

Create a “win” variable that equals to 1 if the team won the game; 0 if the team lost the game; and 0.5 if it was a draw.

Append the “NHL_Home” and “NHL_Away” dataframes to be the new “NHL_Game” dataframe.


Show code
NHL_Away = NHL_game.loc[NHL_game["home_away"].eq("away")].copy()
NHL_Home = NHL_game.loc[NHL_game["home_away"].eq("home")].copy()

NHL_Away = NHL_Away.rename(columns={'ascore': 'goals_for', 'hscore': 'goals_against'})
NHL_Home = NHL_Home.rename(columns={'hscore': 'goals_for', 'ascore': 'goals_against'})

NHL_Away['win'] = np.select([NHL_Away['goals_for']>NHL_Away['goals_against'], NHL_Away['goals_for']<NHL_Away['goals_against']], [1,0], 0.5)
NHL_Home['win'] = np.select([NHL_Home['goals_for']>NHL_Home['goals_against'], NHL_Home['goals_for']<NHL_Home['goals_against']], [1,0], 0.5)


NHL_game = pd.concat([NHL_Away, NHL_Home], ignore_index=True).sort_values(['date', 'gid', 'tid']).reset_index(drop=True)

title: Structural Causal Models & D-Separation in an NBA Pipeline
text:
Objective: Apply the SCM framework (Pearl, 2009) to identify which pipeline signals are causally defensible versus merely correlated. D-separation tests reveal which conditioning sets block confounding paths, ensuring our betting edges are real.
Pipeline Nodes Under Investigation:

Mechanism — Does stakes → effort → score survive conditioning on team quality?
Evaporation — Is the injury impact causal, or confounded by game context (rest games)?
Epistemic — Are opponent adjustments real, or Simpson’s paradox (quality confounding)?
Emergence — Does chemistry cause wins, or do wins create chemistry perception?
Betting Edge — If upstream signals are confounded, edges are too.

Key Technique: D-separation — given a DAG, determine which variables are conditionally independent. If X ⊥ Y | Z but our pipeline assumes X → Y, the signal is spurious.

title: Structural Causal Models & D-Separation in an NBA Pipeline
text:
1. The Full Pipeline DAG
Every variable in our projection → betting pipeline is a node. Every assumed causal relationship is a directed edge. D-separation tells us: given a set of conditioning variables \(Z\), are variables \(X\) and \(Y\) independent?
\[X \perp\!\!\!\perp Y \mid Z \iff \text{every path between } X \text{ and } Y \text{ is blocked by } Z\]
A path is blocked if it contains:

A chain \(A \to B \to C\) where \(B \in Z\) (mediator conditioned on)
A fork \(A \leftarrow B \to C\) where \(B \in Z\) (common cause conditioned on)
A collider \(A \to B \leftarrow C\) where \(B \notin Z\) (collision NOT conditioned on)

If our pipeline treats two variables as causally linked but d-separation says they’re independent given controls, the signal is spurious.


Show code
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  1A. FULL PIPELINE DAG — Define the causal structure
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def build_pipeline_dag():
    """
    Build the full causal DAG for the NBA projection → betting pipeline.
    
    Node categories:
      - EXOGENOUS: schedule, league structure (no parents)
      - CONTEXT:   standings, game context (derived from exogenous)
      - MECHANISM: stakes, effort, rest decisions
      - FEATURES:  rolling stats, adjustments, PBP
      - MODEL:     XGBoost predictions, MC simulation
      - BETTING:   edge, grade, sizing, outcome
    """
    G = nx.DiGraph()
    
    # ── Exogenous variables (no causes within the system) ──
    exog = ["schedule", "league_structure", "team_talent"]
    G.add_nodes_from(exog, layer="exogenous")
    
    # ── Context variables ──
    context = ["standings", "games_remaining", "game_context",
               "is_b2b", "days_rest", "travel"]
    G.add_nodes_from(context, layer="context")
    
    # ── Mechanism variables ──
    mechanism = ["playoff_prob", "stakes", "effort_multiplier",
                 "rest_probability", "tanking_incentive"]
    G.add_nodes_from(mechanism, layer="mechanism")
    
    # ── Feature variables (rolling, adjustments) ──
    features = ["team_rolling_stats", "player_rolling_stats",
                "injury_status", "evaporation_coeff",
                "epistemic_adjustment", "emergence_coeff",
                "lineup_strength", "opponent_quality"]
    G.add_nodes_from(features, layer="features")
    
    # ── Model outputs ──
    model = ["xgb_prediction", "mc_projection", "projected_score"]
    G.add_nodes_from(model, layer="model")
    
    # ── Betting layer ──

        x = layer_x.get(layer, 5)

        edge_color=COLORS["confound"],
        alpha=0.8, arrows=True,
        arrowsize=15, arrowstyle="-|>",
        connectionstyle="arc3,rad=0.15",
        width=2.0, style="dashed",

    # Draw nodes by layer
    for layer, nodes in layer_nodes.items():
        color = layer_colors.get(layer, COLORS["text"])
        nx.draw_networkx_nodes(
            G, pos, nodelist=sorted(nodes), ax=ax,
            node_color=COLORS["bg_card"],

    ]
    ax.legend(handles=legend_patches, loc="lower right",

    ax.set_title("NBA Pipeline — Full Causal DAG",

2. D-Separation Tests — Which Signals Survive?
For each pipeline module, we ask: Is the assumed causal path blocked by confounders we’re not conditioning on?
Using networkx.d_separated(G, X, Y, Z):

X = source variable(s)
Y = target variable(s) (usually bet_outcome or projected_score)
Z = conditioning set (what we control for)

If d-separated → the signal is blocked → our pipeline is using a spurious correlation. If NOT d-separated → there exists an open causal path → signal may be real.


Show code
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  2A. D-SEPARATION TESTS — Systematic pipeline audit
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def test_dsep(G, x_set, y_set, z_set, label=""):
    """Test d-separation and report results.
    Uses nx.is_d_separator (networkx 3.x API).
    Returns True if path is OPEN (not separated), False if BLOCKED.
    """
    x = set(x_set) if isinstance(x_set, (list, set)) else {x_set}
    y = set(y_set) if isinstance(y_set, (list, set)) else {y_set}
    z = set(z_set) if isinstance(z_set, (list, set)) else {z_set}
    
    # is_d_separator returns True when Z separates X from Y (blocked)
    if z:
        separated = nx.is_d_separator(G, x, y, z)
    else:
        # With empty Z, check if there's any path at all
        # If no directed/undirected path exists, they're trivially separated
        separated = nx.is_d_separator(G, x, y, set())
    
    status = "BLOCKED ✗" if separated else "OPEN ✓"
    
    x_str = ", ".join(sorted(x))
    y_str = ", ".join(sorted(y))
    z_str = ", ".join(sorted(z)) if z else "∅ (nothing)"
    
    print(f"  {status}  {label}")
    print(f"           X={x_str}")
    print(f"           Y={y_str}")
    print(f"           Z={{{z_str}}}")
    print()
    return not separated  # True = open path exists

#  2B. D-SEPARATION RESULTS — Visual Summary
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def plot_dsep_summary(results):
    """Heatmap-style summary of which paths survive d-separation."""
    
    modules = list(results.keys())
    # Normalize test names across modules
    all_tests = []
    for mod, tests in results.items():
        for t in tests:
            if t not in all_tests:
                all_tests.append(t)
    
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
    
    # Build matrix
    matrix = np.zeros((len(modules), len(all_tests)))
    for i, mod in enumerate(modules):
        for j, test in enumerate(all_tests):
            val = results[mod].get(test, None)
            if val is None:
                matrix[i, j] = 0.5  # not tested
            elif val:
                matrix[i, j] = 1.0  # open path (causal)
            else:
                matrix[i, j] = 0.0  # blocked (spurious)
    
    # Custom colormap: blocked=magenta, open=cyan
    from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
    cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
        "causal", [COLORS["confound"], COLORS["grid"], COLORS["causal"]]
    )
    
    im = ax.imshow(matrix, cmap=cmap, aspect="auto", vmin=0, vmax=1)
    
    # Labels
    test_labels = [t.replace("_", " ").title() for t in all_tests]
    mod_labels = [m.replace("_", " ").title() for m in modules]
    
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(all_tests)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(test_labels, rotation=30, ha="right", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(modules)))
    ax.set_yticklabels(mod_labels, fontsize=11)
    
    # Annotate cells
    for i in range(len(modules)):
        for j in range(len(all_tests)):
            val = matrix[i, j]
            if val == 1.0:
                txt, color = "OPEN", COLORS["bg_dark"]
            elif val == 0.0:
                txt, color = "BLOCKED", COLORS["text"]
            else:
                txt, color = "N/A", COLORS["grid"]
            ax.text(j, i, txt, ha="center", va="center",
                    fontsize=9, fontweight="bold", color=color)
    
    ax.set_title("D-Separation Audit — Causal Path Status by Conditioning Set",
                 fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", color=COLORS["cyan"], pad=15)
    
    # Legend bar
    cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.02, pad=0.04)
    cbar.set_ticks([0, 0.5, 1])
    cbar.set_ticklabels(["Blocked\n(spurious)", "N/A", "Open\n(causal)"])
    cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=9)
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

plot_dsep_summary(results)

text:
3. Walk-Forward Backtest — Full Physics Engine Causal Tests
The pipeline has 4 physics modules that produce game-level signals. The causal question for each:

Does module X predict outcomes AFTER controlling for team quality?










Module
Signal
Grain
Causal Claim




Mechanism
stakes, effort, tanking, leverage
per-game per-team
High-stakes teams try harder → better outcomes


Emergence
6-component coefficient (chemistry, momentum, fatigue, crowd, referee, nonlinear)
per-game per-team
Nonlinear team effects shift scoring


Evaporation
evap_coeff per player (→ team aggregate)
per-team per-season
Star absence evaporates production


Epistemic
per-dimension adjustments by opponent tier
per-team per-season
Coaching game theory adjusts performance



Walk-Forward CV Design:

Train on seasons 1..N, test on N+1 (2016-2026)
Model A: Quality only (rolling win%)
Model B: Quality + Mechanism
Model C: Quality + Emergence
Model D: Quality + Full Physics (all modules)
Compare OOS AUC/accuracy per fold

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

"""

try:

    for c in df.columns:
        if c not in ("game_id", "game_date", "home_team", "away_team"):

    has_mech = df["stakes_home"].notna()

    has_evap = df["evap_home"].notna()
    has_epist = df["epist_pace_home"].notna()
    
    print(f"Loaded {len(df):,} regular-season games (2014-2026)")
    print(f"  Date range: {df['game_date'].min()} -> {df['game_date'].max()}")
    print(f"  Seasons: {sorted(df['season'].dropna().unique().astype(int).tolist())}")
    print(f"\n  Module coverage:")
    print(f"    Mechanism:   {has_mech.sum():>6,} games ({has_mech.mean():.0%})")

#  3C. COMPUTE ROLLING WIN PCT — Quality Proxy for Each Team
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# We need a quality proxy that doesn't leak future info. Use each team's
# win% PRIOR to each game (expanding window within season).

if len(df) > 0 and "season" in df.columns:
    # Build a long-form record: one row per team per game
    records = []
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        records.append({"game_id": row["game_id"], "game_date": row["game_date"],
                        "season": row["season"], "team": row["home_team"],
                        "won": row["home_won"]})
        records.append({"game_id": row["game_id"], "game_date": row["game_date"],
                        "season": row["season"], "team": row["away_team"],
                        "won": 1 - row["home_won"]})
    
    team_games = pd.DataFrame(records).sort_values(["team", "game_date"])
    
    # Expanding win% PRIOR to each game (shift so current game not included)
    team_games["prior_wins"] = team_games.groupby(["season", "team"])["won"].cumsum().shift(1)
    team_games["prior_games"] = team_games.groupby(["season", "team"]).cumcount()
    # Avoid division by zero: first game of season gets 0.5 (neutral prior)
    team_games["win_pct"] = np.where(
        team_games["prior_games"] > 0,
        team_games["prior_wins"] / team_games["prior_games"],
        0.5
    )
    # Clip to valid range and replace any remaining inf/nan
    team_games["win_pct"] = team_games["win_pct"].clip(0, 1).fillna(0.5)
    
    # Map back to home/away
    wpct_map = team_games.set_index(["game_id", "team"])["win_pct"]
    
    df["win_pct_home"] = df.apply(
        lambda r: wpct_map.get((r["game_id"], r["home_team"]), 0.5), axis=1)
    df["win_pct_away"] = df.apply(
        lambda r: wpct_map.get((r["game_id"], r["away_team"]), 0.5), axis=1)
    df["quality_diff"] = df["win_pct_home"] - df["win_pct_away"]
    
    # Final safety: clip all computed columns
    for col in ["win_pct_home", "win_pct_away", "quality_diff"]:
        df[col] = df[col].clip(-1, 1).fillna(0.5 if "diff" not in col else 0.0)
    
    print(f"✓ Computed prior-game rolling win% for {team_games['team'].nunique()} teams")
    print(f"  Home win_pct range: {df['win_pct_home'].min():.3f} – {df['win_pct_home'].max():.3f}")
    print(f"  Quality diff (H-A): μ={df['quality_diff'].mean():.3f}, σ={df['quality_diff'].std():.3f}")
    print(f"  Any inf/nan in features: {df[['win_pct_home','win_pct_away','quality_diff']].isin([np.inf, -np.inf]).any().any()}")
else:
    print("⚠ No data — skipping win_pct computation")

title: Structural Causal Models & D-Separation in an NBA Pipeline
section: 4. Mechanism Causal Analysis — Does Effort Cause Better Scores?
text:
4. Mechanism Causal Analysis — Does Effort Cause Better Scores?
The confounding problem:
team_talent ──→ standings ──→ playoff_prob ──→ stakes ──→ effort ──→ score
     │                                                               ↑
     └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              (direct quality effect)
Good teams have high standings AND score well. If we naively correlate effort → score, we’re measuring team quality, not effort.
Instrument: games_remaining is set by the league schedule (exogenous). It affects playoff_prob → stakes → effort but doesn’t directly affect game scores. This satisfies the IV exclusion restriction.
SCM Structural Equations:

playoff_prob := f₁(standings, games_remaining, N₁)
stakes := f₂(playoff_prob, game_context, N₂)

effort := f₃(stakes, N₃)
score := f₄(team_talent, opponent, effort, N₄) ← Is effort’s coefficient nonzero?

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  4A. MECHANISM — Focused Sub-DAG Visualization
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def draw_mechanism_subdag():
    """Draw the mechanism-specific causal sub-DAG."""
    G = nx.DiGraph()
    
    nodes = {
        "team_quality":    (0, 2),
        "games_remaining": (0, 0),
        "standings":       (2, 2),
        "playoff_prob":    (4, 1),
        "stakes":          (6, 1),
        "effort":          (8, 1),
        "actual_score":    (10, 1),
        "market_line":     (8, 3),
        "model_edge":      (10, 3),
        "bet_outcome":     (12, 2),
    }
    
    for n, p in nodes.items():
        G.add_node(n)
    
    # Causal edges
    causal = [
        ("games_remaining", "playoff_prob"),
        ("standings", "playoff_prob"),
        ("playoff_prob", "stakes"),
        ("stakes", "effort"),
        ("effort", "actual_score"),
        ("actual_score", "bet_outcome"),
        ("market_line", "bet_outcome"),
        ("model_edge", "bet_outcome"),
    ]
    
    # Confounding edges
    confound = [
        ("team_quality", "standings"),
        ("team_quality", "actual_score"),
    ]
    
    # IV edge (instrument)
    iv = [
        ("games_remaining", "playoff_prob"),
    ]
    
    G.add_edges_from(causal)
    G.add_edges_from(confound)
    
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 7))

#  4B. MECHANISM — Empirical Partial Correlation Test
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
from scipy import stats

def partial_corr(df, x, y, controls):
    """Partial correlation via OLS residualization."""
    from numpy.linalg import lstsq
    
    cols = [x, y] + controls
    mask = df[cols].dropna()
    if len(mask) < 30:
        return np.nan, np.nan, len(mask)
    
    X_ctrl = mask[controls].values
    X_ctrl = np.column_stack([X_ctrl, np.ones(len(X_ctrl))])
    
    coef_x, _, _, _ = lstsq(X_ctrl, mask[x].values, rcond=None)
    resid_x = mask[x].values - X_ctrl @ coef_x
    
    coef_y, _, _, _ = lstsq(X_ctrl, mask[y].values, rcond=None)
    resid_y = mask[y].values - X_ctrl @ coef_y
    
    r, p = stats.pearsonr(resid_x, resid_y)
    return r, p, len(mask)

        if x_var not in df.columns or y_var not in df.columns:
            continue
        raw_r, raw_p, raw_n = partial_corr(df, x_var, y_var, [])
        ctrl_r, ctrl_p, ctrl_n = partial_corr(df, x_var, y_var, available_controls)

    print("  - If 'Ctrl r' significantly nonzero: mechanism has CAUSAL effect")

text:
5. Evaporation Causal Analysis — Injury Impact or Rest Game Artifact?
The confounding problem:
clinched_status ──→ star_rests ──→ score_drops
       │                              ↑
       └──────────────────────────────┘
       (team also coasts in low-stakes game)
When a star sits, the team’s evaporation coefficient says “they’ll score X fewer points.” But if the star only sits in games the team doesn’t care about, the scoring drop might be from reduced effort, not from missing the player.
D-separation fix: Condition on game_context (stakes, B2B status). If evaporation’s effect vanishes → it was measuring effort, not player impact.

6. Epistemic Adjustment — Simpson’s Paradox Test
The confounding problem:
opponent_quality ──→ epistemic_adjustment ──→ game_score
       │                                         ↑
       └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
             (better opponents = lower scores regardless)
The epistemic module says “this team adjusts their pace/offense against elite opponents.” But if the team scores less against elite opponents simply because those opponents are good, the “adjustment” is just measuring opponent strength.
Simpson’s Paradox: The overall correlation might show adjustments predict scoring, but within each opponent tier, the effect could vanish or even reverse.

#  6A. EPISTEMIC — Simpson's Paradox Detection

                f"n={int(row['n'])}\n{row['win_rate']:.1%}",
                ha="center", fontsize=8, color=COLORS["text"])
    
    ax.axhline(0.5, color=COLORS["confound"], linestyle="--", alpha=0.7)
    ax.set_xticks(x_pos)
    ax.set_xticklabels(tier_stats["opp_tier"], fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("Home Win Rate")
    ax.set_title("Home Win Rate by Opponent Tier\n(Does performance depend on opponent?)",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2, axis="y")
    
    # --- Panel 3: Partial correlation — Home quality vs margin, controlling opp quality ---
    ax = axes[2]
    
    tier_corrs = []
    for tier in df_epist["opp_tier"].unique():
        subset = df_epist[df_epist["opp_tier"] == tier]
        if len(subset) > 20:
            r_raw, p_raw = stats.pearsonr(subset["win_pct_home"], subset["home_margin"])
            r_ctrl, p_ctrl, n_ctrl = partial_corr(subset, "win_pct_home", "home_margin",
                                                    ["win_pct_away"])
            tier_corrs.append({
                "tier": tier,
                "r_raw": r_raw,
                "r_controlled": r_ctrl if not np.isnan(r_ctrl) else 0,
                "n": len(subset),
            })
    
    if tier_corrs:
        tc_df = pd.DataFrame(tier_corrs)
        x_pos = range(len(tc_df))
        width = 0.35
        
        ax.bar([x - width/2 for x in x_pos], tc_df["r_raw"],
               width, color=COLORS["cyan"], alpha=0.8, label="Raw r")
        ax.bar([x + width/2 for x in x_pos], tc_df["r_controlled"],
               width, color=COLORS["gold"], alpha=0.8, label="Controlled r")
        
        ax.axhline(0, color=COLORS["grid"], linewidth=1)
        ax.set_xticks(list(x_pos))
        ax.set_xticklabels(tc_df["tier"], fontsize=10)
        ax.set_ylabel("Correlation (r)")
        ax.set_title("Home Quality → Margin\nRaw vs Controlled (by Opp Tier)",
                     fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
        ax.legend(fontsize=8, facecolor=COLORS["bg_card"], labelcolor=COLORS["text"])
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2, axis="y")
    
    fig.suptitle("Epistemic — Simpson's Paradox & Opponent Quality Confounding",
                 fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", color=COLORS["cyan"])
    plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.95))
    plt.show()
    
    # Print Simpson's Paradox check
    print("\n  SIMPSON'S PARADOX CHECK:")
    print("  " + "-" * 50)
    overall_r, overall_p = stats.pearsonr(df_epist["win_pct_away"], df_epist["home_margin"])
    print(f"  Overall correlation (opp_quality → home_margin): r={overall_r:+.3f}, p={overall_p:.4f}")
    for _, row in pd.DataFrame(tier_corrs).iterrows():
        direction = "same" if np.sign(row["r_controlled"]) == np.sign(overall_r) else "REVERSED"
        print(f"  {row['tier']:>10}: r_ctrl={row['r_controlled']:+.3f} (n={int(row['n'])}) [{direction}]")
    
    reversal = any(np.sign(r["r_controlled"]) != np.sign(overall_r) for _, r in pd.DataFrame(tier_corrs).iterrows())
    if reversal:
        print("\n  SIMPSON'S PARADOX DETECTED — direction reverses within tiers!")
    else:
        print("\n  No Simpson's Paradox — effect direction consistent across tiers")
else:
    print("Insufficient opponent quality data for epistemic analysis")

title: Structural Causal Models & D-Separation in an NBA Pipeline
text:
8. Structural Equations — Fitting the SCM
Now we fit the actual structural equations from the DAG. Each node gets a function of its parents + noise. This moves from qualitative (DAG) to quantitative (how strong is each causal effect?).
\[X_j := f_j(\text{Parents}(X_j), N_j)\]
We use OLS for interpretability — the coefficients are the causal effects under the SCM assumptions.


Show code
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  8. STRUCTURAL EQUATIONS — Fit the SCM
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

if len(df) > 50:
    print("=" * 70)
    print("  STRUCTURAL CAUSAL MODEL — Fitted Equations")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    equations = {}
    
    # Equation 1: home_score := f(win_pct_home, win_pct_away, effort_home, stakes_home)
    eq1_cols = ["win_pct_home", "win_pct_away", "effort_home", "stakes_home"]
    eq1_target = "home_score"
    eq1_data = df[eq1_cols + [eq1_target]].dropna()
    
    if len(eq1_data) > 30:
        model1 = LinearRegression().fit(eq1_data[eq1_cols], eq1_data[eq1_target])
        r2 = model1.score(eq1_data[eq1_cols], eq1_data[eq1_target])
        residuals1 = eq1_data[eq1_target] - model1.predict(eq1_data[eq1_cols])
        
        print(f"\n  Eq 1: home_score := f(quality, effort, stakes) + N")
        print(f"  R2 = {r2:.4f}, n = {len(eq1_data)}")
        print(f"  Residual std = {residuals1.std():.2f} pts")
        print(f"  {'_' * 50}")
        for col, coef in zip(eq1_cols, model1.coef_):
            sig = "***" if abs(coef) > 1.0 else "**" if abs(coef) > 0.5 else "*" if abs(coef) > 0.1 else ""
            print(f"    {col:25s} B = {coef:+8.3f} {sig}")
        print(f"    {'intercept':25s} B0 = {model1.intercept_:+8.3f}")
        equations["home_score"] = {
            "parents": eq1_cols, "coefs": dict(zip(eq1_cols, model1.coef_)),
            "intercept": model1.intercept_, "r2": r2, "resid_std": residuals1.std(),
        }
    
    # Equation 2: home_margin := f(effort_diff, stakes_diff, quality_diff)
    df["stakes_diff"] = (df["stakes_home"] - df["stakes_away"])
    df["effort_diff"] = df["effort_home"] - df["effort_away"]
    eq2_cols = ["effort_diff", "stakes_diff", "quality_diff", "win_pct_home", "win_pct_away"]
    eq2_target = "home_margin"
    eq2_data = df[eq2_cols + [eq2_target]].dropna()
    
    if len(eq2_data) > 30:
        model2 = LinearRegression().fit(eq2_data[eq2_cols], eq2_data[eq2_target])
        r2_2 = model2.score(eq2_data[eq2_cols], eq2_data[eq2_target])
        residuals2 = eq2_data[eq2_target] - model2.predict(eq2_data[eq2_cols])
        
        print(f"\n  Eq 2: home_margin := f(effort_diff, stakes_diff, quality) + N")
        print(f"  R2 = {r2_2:.4f}, n = {len(eq2_data)}")
        print(f"  Residual std = {residuals2.std():.2f} pts")
        print(f"  {'_' * 50}")
        for col, coef in zip(eq2_cols, model2.coef_):
            sig = "***" if abs(coef) > 1.0 else "**" if abs(coef) > 0.5 else "*" if abs(coef) > 0.1 else ""
            print(f"    {col:25s} B = {coef:+8.3f} {sig}")
        print(f"    {'intercept':25s} B0 = {model2.intercept_:+8.3f}")
        equations["home_margin"] = {
            "parents": eq2_cols, "coefs": dict(zip(eq2_cols, model2.coef_)),
            "intercept": model2.intercept_, "r2": r2_2, "resid_std": residuals2.std(),
        }
    
    # ── Visualize structural equation coefficients ──
    if equations:
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(equations), figsize=(8 * len(equations), 5))
        if len(equations) == 1:
            axes = [axes]
        
        for ax, (eq_name, eq_info) in zip(axes, equations.items()):
            coefs = eq_info["coefs"]
            names = list(coefs.keys())
            vals = list(coefs.values())
            colors = [COLORS["causal"] if v > 0 else COLORS["confound"] for v in vals]
            
            ax.barh(range(len(names)), vals, color=colors, alpha=0.8,
                    edgecolor=COLORS["bg_dark"])
            ax.set_yticks(range(len(names)))
            ax.set_yticklabels([n.replace("_", " ") for n in names], fontsize=10)
            ax.axvline(0, color=COLORS["grid"], linewidth=1)
            ax.set_xlabel("Coefficient (B)")
            ax.set_title(f"SCM Equation: {eq_name}\nR2={eq_info['r2']:.3f}",
                         fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
            ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2, axis="x")
            
            for i, v in enumerate(vals):
                ax.text(v + 0.05 * np.sign(v), i, f"{v:+.3f}",
                        va="center", fontsize=9, color=COLORS["text"])
        
        fig.suptitle("Fitted Structural Equations — Causal Effect Sizes",
                     fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", color=COLORS["cyan"])
        plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.95))
        plt.show()
    
    print("\n  INTERPRETATION:")
    print("  " + "-" * 50)
    print("  B(effort) close to 0 after controlling quality -> effort signal is confounded")
    print("  B(effort) significantly nonzero -> effort has CAUSAL effect beyond quality")
    print("  B(win_pct) dominates -> team quality is the real driver")
else:
    print("Insufficient data for structural equations")

9. Final Conclusion — Causal Audit of the NBA Physics Engine

Module-Level Causal Verdict









Module
AUC Lift
Causal?
Interpretation




Emergence
+4.6%
YES
Lineup chemistry, fatigue cascade, momentum, and crowd effects carry genuine out-of-sample predictive signal that survives controlling for team quality. Dominant module — 76% of full model’s coefficient mass.


Mechanism
+0.5%
Marginal
Stakes and effort add a small signal but mostly proxy team quality. The effort multiplier’s narrow range (0.986-1.012) limits its discriminative power.


Evaporation
~0.3%
Weak
Directionally correct (teams with higher star-evaporation risk underperform) but the signal is absorbed by emergence’s fatigue cascade. Season-level grain too coarse for game-level prediction.


Epistemic
~0.2%
Weak
Coaching adjustments by opponent tier are real in-sample but don’t generalize well out-of-sample. Likely overfits to historical matchup patterns that shift year to year.





D-Separation Validation
All 5 theoretical d-separation tests confirmed open causal paths from each physics module to outcomes — the DAG structure permits causal effects. The walk-forward CV then empirically measured which paths carry actual signal vs. which are confounded by team quality.


Key Structural Findings

Emergence is the engine. The 6-component emergence coefficient (chemistry + momentum + fatigue + crowd + referee + nonlinear) is the only module that consistently lifts AUC across seasons. It wins 6/9 folds outright.
Full Physics slightly overfits. Model D (38 features) loses to Model C (17 features) in 6/9 folds. The mechanism, evaporation, and epistemic features add noise that offsets their marginal signal. A regularized or feature-selected full model may recover this.
Mechanism’s effort multiplier is near-degenerate. Range of 0.986-1.012 means ~1.3% max effect — too narrow to overcome team quality confounding. Stakes has better variance but correlates with team talent.
The confounding problem is real. Partial correlations show raw mechanism-outcome correlations shrink 40-70% after controlling for team quality. The naive causal effect of effort on win rate is largely team quality in disguise.
Intervention simulation confirms: Stratified do(effort=high) vs do(effort=low) shows the naive effect is mostly absorbed by quality tiers. The residual causal effect is small but nonzero.



Recommendations for the Pipeline

Prioritize emergence calibration. This is where predictive value lives. Invest in lineup chemistry data quality and fatigue cascade accuracy.
Demote mechanism weight in the Monte Carlo simulation. Its contribution is marginal after quality adjustment.
Consider dropping epistemic from game-level prediction — use it only for season-level tendency analysis.
Upgrade evaporation to game-level grain (per-game injury status) rather than season-level aggregates to unlock its full potential.
Feature selection before the full physics model would likely outperform both Model C and Model D.



Show code
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  9. FINAL SUMMARY — Intervention Simulation (do-calculus)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Demonstrate the SCM interventional question:
#   P(bet_outcome=win | do(effort=high)) vs P(bet_outcome=win | do(effort=low))

if len(df) > 50 and "effort_home" in df.columns and df["effort_home"].notna().sum() > 30:
    
    df_int = df.dropna(subset=["effort_home", "home_won", "win_pct_home", "win_pct_away"])
    
    # Split into high/low effort (median)
    median_effort = df_int["effort_home"].median()
    high_eff = df_int[df_int["effort_home"] >= median_effort]
    low_eff = df_int[df_int["effort_home"] < median_effort]
    
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 5))
    
    # --- Panel 1: Naive intervention (no controls) ---
    ax = axes[0]
    naive = pd.DataFrame({
        "Outcome": ["Win Rate", "Avg Margin"],
        "High Effort": [high_eff["home_won"].mean(), high_eff["home_margin"].mean()],
        "Low Effort": [low_eff["home_won"].mean(), low_eff["home_margin"].mean()],
    })
    x_pos = np.arange(2)
    width = 0.35
    ax.bar(x_pos - width/2, naive["High Effort"], width, color=COLORS["cyan"],
           alpha=0.8, label=f"High Effort (n={len(high_eff):,})")
    ax.bar(x_pos + width/2, naive["Low Effort"], width, color=COLORS["magenta"],
           alpha=0.8, label=f"Low Effort (n={len(low_eff):,})")
    ax.axhline(0.5, color=COLORS["gold"], linestyle="--", alpha=0.7)
    ax.set_xticks(x_pos)
    ax.set_xticklabels(naive["Outcome"])
    ax.set_ylabel("Rate / Points")
    ax.set_title("Naive: do(effort=high) vs do(effort=low)\n(NO confound control)",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8, facecolor=COLORS["bg_card"], labelcolor=COLORS["text"])
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2, axis="y")
    
    # --- Panel 2: Stratified intervention (control for quality) ---
    ax = axes[1]
    df_int = df_int.copy()
    df_int["quality_tier"] = pd.qcut(df_int["win_pct_home"], q=3,
                                      labels=["Low Q", "Mid Q", "High Q"],
                                      duplicates="drop")
    
    strat_results = []
    for tier in df_int["quality_tier"].cat.categories:
        subset = df_int[df_int["quality_tier"] == tier]
        h = subset[subset["effort_home"] >= median_effort]
        l = subset[subset["effort_home"] < median_effort]
        if len(h) > 5 and len(l) > 5:
            strat_results.append({
                "tier": tier,
                "high_win": h["home_won"].mean(),
                "low_win": l["home_won"].mean(),
                "diff": h["home_won"].mean() - l["home_won"].mean(),
                "n_high": len(h),
                "n_low": len(l),
            })
    
    if strat_results:
        sr = pd.DataFrame(strat_results)
        x_pos = np.arange(len(sr))
        ax.bar(x_pos - width/2, sr["high_win"], width, color=COLORS["cyan"], alpha=0.8, label="High Effort")
        ax.bar(x_pos + width/2, sr["low_win"], width, color=COLORS["magenta"], alpha=0.8, label="Low Effort")
        ax.axhline(0.5, color=COLORS["gold"], linestyle="--", alpha=0.7)
        ax.set_xticks(x_pos)
        ax.set_xticklabels(sr["tier"])
        ax.set_ylabel("Win Rate")
        ax.set_title("Stratified: do(effort) | team_quality\n(Causal effect within quality tiers)",
                     fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
        ax.legend(fontsize=8, facecolor=COLORS["bg_card"], labelcolor=COLORS["text"])
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2, axis="y")
        ax.set_ylim(0.2, 0.85)
    
    # --- Panel 3: Effect size comparison ---
    ax = axes[2]
    naive_diff = high_eff["home_won"].mean() - low_eff["home_won"].mean()
    causal_diffs = [r["diff"] for r in strat_results] if strat_results else [0]
    avg_causal = np.mean(causal_diffs)
    
    bars = ax.bar(["Naive\n(confounded)", "Stratified\n(causal estimate)"],
                   [naive_diff, avg_causal],
                   color=[COLORS["magenta"], COLORS["causal"]],
                   alpha=0.8, edgecolor=COLORS["bg_dark"], width=0.5)
    ax.axhline(0, color=COLORS["grid"], linewidth=1)
    ax.set_ylabel("Win Rate Difference (High - Low Effort)")
    ax.set_title("Effort Causal Effect:\nNaive vs Deconfounded",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2, axis="y")
    
    for i, (v, label) in enumerate(zip([naive_diff, avg_causal],
                                        ["confounded", "causal"])):
        ax.text(i, v + 0.005 * np.sign(v) if v != 0 else 0.005, f"{v:+.3f}",
                ha="center", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=COLORS["text"])
    
    fig.suptitle("Interventional Analysis — do(effort=high) vs do(effort=low)",
                 fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", color=COLORS["cyan"])
    plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.95))
    plt.show()
    
    print(f"\n  CAUSAL EFFECT ESTIMATE:")
    print(f"  {'_' * 45}")
    print(f"  Naive (confounded):     {naive_diff:+.4f} win rate difference")
    print(f"  Stratified (causal):    {avg_causal:+.4f} win rate difference")
    reduction = 1 - abs(avg_causal) / abs(naive_diff) if naive_diff != 0 else 0
    print(f"  Confounding absorbed:   {reduction:.0%} of the naive effect was team quality")
    
    if abs(avg_causal) < 0.02:
        print(f"\n  VERDICT: Effort effect is NEGLIGIBLE after deconfounding.")
        print(f"     The mechanism module's effort multiplier may be proxying team quality.")
    elif abs(avg_causal) > 0.05:
        print(f"\n  VERDICT: Effort has a REAL causal effect ({avg_causal:+.3f}).")
        print(f"     The mechanism module adds genuine predictive value.")
    else:
        print(f"\n  VERDICT: Effort effect is MARGINAL ({avg_causal:+.3f}).")
        print(f"     Need more data or IV estimation to confirm.")
else:
    print("Insufficient data for intervention simulation")

title: Pricing Consistency & Data Quality Analysis
text:
4 Price consistency (CV) across snaps 1–4
Uses calendar price (daily rate from calendar_cleaned), aggregated to a per-snapshot ADR for each listing, then CV measured across those 4 snapshot ADRs. Restricted to listings also present in snaps 5–6 (the imputable universe).
CV = stddev(snapshot_ADR) / mean(snapshot_ADR).


Show code
sql = f"""
WITH late_listings AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT listing_id, host_id
    FROM {TABLE}
    WHERE snapshot_date IN ({late_in})
),
snap_adr AS (
    -- Per-listing per-snapshot ADR from calendar
    SELECT c.listing_id, c.host_id, c.snapshot_date,
           AVG(c.price) AS adr
    FROM {CAL_TABLE} c
    INNER JOIN late_listings l USING (listing_id, host_id)
    WHERE c.snapshot_date IN ({early_in})
      AND c.price IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c.listing_id, c.host_id, c.snapshot_date
),
listing_cv AS (
    SELECT
        listing_id, host_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT snapshot_date)                                              AS n_obs,
        ROUND(AVG(adr)::numeric, 2)                                                AS mean_adr,
        ROUND(STDDEV(adr)::numeric, 2)                                             AS std_adr,
        MIN(adr)                                                                   AS min_adr,
        MAX(adr)                                                                   AS max_adr,
        CASE WHEN AVG(adr) > 0
             THEN ROUND((COALESCE(STDDEV(adr), 0) / AVG(adr))::numeric, 4)
             ELSE 0 END                                                            AS cv
    FROM snap_adr
    GROUP BY listing_id, host_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT snapshot_date) >= 2
)
SELECT
    n_obs,
    COUNT(*)                                                                       AS listings,
    ROUND(AVG(cv)::numeric,  4)                                                    AS avg_cv,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cv)::numeric, 4)            AS p25_cv,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cv)::numeric, 4)            AS median_cv,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cv)::numeric, 4)            AS p75_cv,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.90) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cv)::numeric, 4)            AS p90_cv,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cv = 0                    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                     AS cv_zero,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cv > 0    AND cv <= 0.05  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                     AS cv_le_5pct,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cv > 0.05 AND cv <= 0.15  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                     AS cv_5_to_15pct,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cv > 0.15 AND cv <= 0.30  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                     AS cv_15_to_30pct,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cv > 0.30                 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                     AS cv_gt_30pct
FROM listing_cv
GROUP BY n_obs
ORDER BY n_obs
"""

             ELSE 0 END AS cv
    FROM snap_adr
    GROUP BY listing_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT snapshot_date) = 4
),
low_cv  AS (SELECT listing_id FROM listing_cv WHERE cv <= 0.05),

SELECT s.listing_id, s.snapshot_date::text AS snap, s.adr,
       CASE WHEN lc.listing_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'low_cv' ELSE 'high_cv' END AS grp
FROM snap_adr s
INNER JOIN (SELECT listing_id FROM low_cv UNION ALL SELECT listing_id FROM high_cv) u
    USING (listing_id)

ORDER BY grp, s.listing_id, s.snapshot_date
"""

}

        ax.plot(g['snap'], g['adr'].clip(upper=y_cap), color=cfg['line_clr'],
                alpha=alph, linewidth=0.7)

    # bold median + P25/P75 band
    stats = sub.groupby('snap')['adr'].agg(['median', 'mean',
        lambda x: x.quantile(0.25), lambda x: x.quantile(0.75)]
    ).reset_index()
    stats.columns = ['snap', 'median', 'mean', 'p25', 'p75']
    stats = stats.sort_values('snap')

    ax.fill_between(stats['snap'], stats['p25'], stats['p75'],

    ax.plot(stats['snap'], stats['median'], color=cfg['med_clr'],
            linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=6, label='Median ADR', zorder=5)
    ax.plot(stats['snap'], stats['mean'], color=cfg['med_clr'],
            linewidth=1.5, marker='s', markersize=4, linestyle='--',
            label='Mean ADR', zorder=5, alpha=0.7)

    ax.set_ylim(bottom=0, top=y_cap)
    ax.set_title(f"{cfg['title']} (n={n:,})", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlabel('Snapshot')
    ax.set_ylabel('ADR ($/night)')
    ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=30)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper right')

    # annotate median values
    for _, row in stats.iterrows():
        ax.annotate(f'${row["median"]:.0f}', (row['snap'], row['median']),
                    textcoords='offset points', xytext=(0, 8),
                    ha='center', fontsize=7.5, color=cfg['med_clr'], fontweight='bold')

fig.suptitle('ADR trajectories across early snapshots — imputable listings\n'
             '(faint lines = individual listings, y-axis capped at P99)',
             fontsize=11)

    FROM {CAL_TABLE} c
    INNER JOIN late_listings l USING (listing_id, host_id)
    WHERE c.snapshot_date IN ({early_in})
      AND c.price IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c.listing_id, c.host_id, c.snapshot_date
),
listing_cv AS (
    SELECT
        CASE WHEN AVG(adr) > 0
             THEN COALESCE(STDDEV(adr), 0) / AVG(adr)
             ELSE 0 END AS cv
    FROM snap_adr
    GROUP BY listing_id, host_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT snapshot_date) >= 2
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*)                                                                      AS n_with_2plus_obs,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cv)::numeric, 4)           AS median_cv,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN cv <= 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1)    AS pct_cv_le_5,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN cv <= 0.15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1)    AS pct_cv_le_15,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN cv >  0.30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1)    AS pct_cv_gt_30
FROM listing_cv
"""
df_dec = pd.read_sql(sql, engine)
print('=== Calendar-price CV summary (imputable listings with >= 2 observations) ===')
print(df_dec.to_string(index=False))
print()
print('Decision thresholds:')
print('  beds / bathrooms : impute if pct_beds_constant > 95% AND pct_baths_constant > 95%')
print('  price (ADR)      : impute if median_cv < 0.10 AND pct_cv_gt_30 < 15%')
print('                     otherwise treat as high-risk -- consider dropping or')
print('                     using mean ADR as a flagged lower-quality feature.')

text:
6 Write imputation table to DB
Creates airbnb_features.listing_snapshot_imputed – one row per (snapshot_date, listing_id) across all 6 snapshots.

adr: actual from overall_listing_metrics.adr_365 (snaps 1-4) or carried forward from the most recent non-null snapshot (snaps 5-6).
beds / bathrooms: same carry-forward logic from listings_property_cleaned.
price_imputed: TRUE only for rows in snaps 5-6 where no actual ADR exists.
source_snapshot: the snapshot whose value was carried forward (NULL for actual rows).



Show code
# Section 6: Write imputation table to DB
sql_create = """
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS airbnb_features;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS airbnb_features.listing_snapshot_imputed (
    snapshot_date   date,
    listing_id      bigint,
    host_id         bigint,
    adr             numeric(10,2),
    beds            numeric(10,2),
    bathrooms       numeric(10,2),
    price_imputed   boolean        NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    source_snapshot date,
    PRIMARY KEY (snapshot_date, listing_id)
);

TRUNCATE airbnb_features.listing_snapshot_imputed;

INSERT INTO airbnb_features.listing_snapshot_imputed
WITH all_listings AS (
    -- All (snapshot_date, listing_id, host_id) across all 6 snapshots
    SELECT DISTINCT snapshot_date, listing_id, host_id
    FROM airbnb_cleaned.listings_property_cleaned
),
actual_adr AS (
    SELECT snapshot_date, listing_id, host_id, adr_365 AS adr
    FROM airbnb_analytics.overall_listing_metrics
    WHERE adr_365 IS NOT NULL
),
actual_struct AS (
    SELECT snapshot_date, listing_id, host_id, beds, bathrooms
    FROM airbnb_cleaned.listings_property_cleaned
    WHERE beds IS NOT NULL OR bathrooms IS NOT NULL
),
-- For each listing, carry forward from the most recent snapshot with a non-null value
latest_adr AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (listing_id, host_id)
        listing_id, host_id, snapshot_date AS source_snap, adr
    FROM actual_adr
    ORDER BY listing_id, host_id, snapshot_date DESC
),
latest_struct AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (listing_id, host_id)
        listing_id, host_id, snapshot_date AS source_snap, beds, bathrooms
    FROM actual_struct
    ORDER BY listing_id, host_id, snapshot_date DESC
)
SELECT
    a.snapshot_date,
    a.listing_id,
    a.host_id,
    COALESCE(act_adr.adr,     la.adr)         AS adr,
    COALESCE(act_s.beds,      ls.beds)         AS beds,
    COALESCE(act_s.bathrooms, ls.bathrooms)    AS bathrooms,
    -- price_imputed = late snapshot AND no actual ADR
    (a.snapshot_date IN ('2025-06-24', '2025-09-26')
     AND act_adr.adr IS NULL)                  AS price_imputed,
    CASE WHEN a.snapshot_date IN ('2025-06-24', '2025-09-26')
              AND act_adr.adr IS NULL
         THEN la.source_snap
         ELSE NULL
    END                                        AS source_snapshot
FROM all_listings a
LEFT JOIN actual_adr    act_adr ON act_adr.snapshot_date = a.snapshot_date
                                AND act_adr.listing_id   = a.listing_id
LEFT JOIN actual_struct act_s   ON act_s.snapshot_date   = a.snapshot_date
                                AND act_s.listing_id     = a.listing_id
LEFT JOIN latest_adr    la      ON la.listing_id = a.listing_id
                                AND la.host_id   = a.host_id
LEFT JOIN latest_struct ls      ON ls.listing_id = a.listing_id
                                AND ls.host_id   = a.host_id;
"""

with engine.begin() as conn:
    conn.execute(text(sql_create))

print("airbnb_features.listing_snapshot_imputed written successfully.")

    FROM airbnb_features.listing_snapshot_imputed

""", engine)

title: Pricing Consistency & Data Quality Analysis
text:
7 ADR outlier detection
Flag listings whose ADR is statistically extreme within each snapshot using two complementary methods:

7a Cross-sectional (IQR): ADR below Q1 − 1.5×IQR or above Q3 + 1.5×IQR within the same snapshot.
7b Temporal spikes: For listings present in consecutive snapshots, |% change| in adr_90 exceeding 50 % snapshot-over-snapshot.



Show code
METRICS_TABLE = 'airbnb_analytics.overall_listing_metrics'

# --- 7a: IQR-based ADR outliers per snapshot (using adr_90) ---
sql_iqr = f"""
WITH stats AS (
    SELECT
        snapshot_date,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY adr_90) AS q1,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY adr_90) AS q3
    FROM {METRICS_TABLE}
    WHERE adr_90 IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY snapshot_date
)
SELECT
    m.snapshot_date::text AS snapshot_date,
    m.listing_id,
    m.host_id,
    m.adr_90,
    s.q1, s.q3, (s.q3 - s.q1) AS iqr,
    CASE
        WHEN m.adr_90 < s.q1 - 1.5 * (s.q3 - s.q1) THEN 'low'
        WHEN m.adr_90 > s.q3 + 1.5 * (s.q3 - s.q1) THEN 'high'
        ELSE NULL
    END AS adr_outlier_dir
FROM {METRICS_TABLE} m
JOIN stats s USING (snapshot_date)
WHERE m.adr_90 IS NOT NULL
"""
df_adr = pd.read_sql(sql_iqr, engine)
df_adr_outliers = df_adr[df_adr['adr_outlier_dir'].notna()]

# Summary table
adr_summary = (
    df_adr.groupby('snapshot_date')
    .agg(
        total=('listing_id', 'count'),
        outlier_low=('adr_outlier_dir', lambda s: (s == 'low').sum()),
        outlier_high=('adr_outlier_dir', lambda s: (s == 'high').sum()),
    )
    .assign(
        pct_outlier=lambda d: round(100 * (d.outlier_low + d.outlier_high) / d.total, 1)
    )
)
print('=== ADR outliers (IQR method, adr_90) ===')
print(adr_summary.to_string())
print()

# Box plot per snapshot
snaps_sorted = sorted(df_adr['snapshot_date'].unique())
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
box_data = [df_adr.loc[df_adr['snapshot_date'] == s, 'adr_90'].dropna().values
            for s in snaps_sorted]
bp = ax.boxplot(box_data, tick_labels=snaps_sorted, showfliers=True,
                flierprops=dict(marker='.', markersize=3, alpha=0.4))
ax.set_ylabel('ADR ($/night) -- 90-day window')
ax.set_xlabel('Snapshot')
ax.set_title('ADR distribution by snapshot (box = IQR, whiskers = 1.5×IQR)\n'
             'Dots beyond whiskers are flagged outliers')
ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=25)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# --- 7b: Temporal ADR spikes (snapshot-over-snapshot % change) ---
sql_temporal = f"""
WITH ordered AS (
    SELECT
        snapshot_date,
        listing_id,
        host_id,
        adr_90,
        LAG(adr_90) OVER (PARTITION BY listing_id ORDER BY snapshot_date) AS prev_adr_90,
        LAG(snapshot_date) OVER (PARTITION BY listing_id ORDER BY snapshot_date) AS prev_snapshot
    FROM {METRICS_TABLE}
    WHERE adr_90 IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    snapshot_date::text AS snapshot_date,
    listing_id,
    host_id,
    adr_90,
    prev_adr_90,
    prev_snapshot::text AS prev_snapshot,
    ROUND(((adr_90 - prev_adr_90) / NULLIF(prev_adr_90, 0) * 100)::numeric, 1) AS pct_change
FROM ordered
WHERE prev_adr_90 IS NOT NULL
"""
df_spikes = pd.read_sql(sql_temporal, engine)
df_spikes['is_spike'] = df_spikes['pct_change'].abs() > 50

spike_summary = (
    df_spikes.groupby('snapshot_date')
    .agg(
        pairs=('listing_id', 'count'),
        spikes=('is_spike', 'sum'),
    )
    .assign(pct_spike=lambda d: round(100 * d.spikes / d.pairs, 1))
)
print('=== Temporal ADR spikes (|% change| > 50%) ===')
print(spike_summary.to_string())
print()

# Histogram of % changes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
clipped = df_spikes['pct_change'].clip(-200, 200)
ax.hist(clipped, bins=80, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.4, color='#4C72B0')
ax.axvline(-50, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.4, label='-50% threshold')
ax.axvline( 50, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.4, label='+50% threshold')
ax.axvline(  0, color='grey', linestyle='-', linewidth=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel('ADR % change (snapshot over snapshot, clipped to ±200%)')
ax.set_ylabel('Number of listing-pairs')
ax.set_title('Snapshot-over-snapshot ADR change distribution\n'
             'Red dashed = ±50% spike threshold')
ax.legend()
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
print(f"Total listing-pairs: {len(df_spikes):,}")
print(f"Spikes (|change| > 50%): {df_spikes['is_spike'].sum():,} "
      f"({100 * df_spikes['is_spike'].mean():.1f}%)")

text:
8 Occupancy anomalies
Two extremes worth flagging:

Saturated (occ_90 >= 0.95): Near-100 % occupancy likely reflects a host-blocked calendar rather than genuine bookings.
Zero (occ_90 == 0 with data present): Listing has calendar data but zero booked days — inactive or withdrawn from market.



Show code
sql_occ = f"""
SELECT
    snapshot_date::text AS snapshot_date,
    listing_id,
    host_id,
    occ_90,
    days_90,
    booked_90,
    adr_90
FROM {METRICS_TABLE}
WHERE days_90 > 0
"""
df_occ = pd.read_sql(sql_occ, engine)
df_occ['occ_flag'] = np.where(
    df_occ['occ_90'] >= 0.95, 'saturated',
    np.where(df_occ['occ_90'] == 0, 'zero', 'normal'))

occ_summary = (
    df_occ.groupby('snapshot_date')
    .agg(
        total=('listing_id', 'count'),
        saturated=('occ_flag', lambda s: (s == 'saturated').sum()),
        zero=('occ_flag', lambda s: (s == 'zero').sum()),
        normal=('occ_flag', lambda s: (s == 'normal').sum()),
    )
    .assign(
        pct_saturated=lambda d: round(100 * d.saturated / d.total, 1),
        pct_zero=lambda d: round(100 * d.zero / d.total, 1),
    )
)
print('=== Occupancy anomalies (90-day window) ===')
print(occ_summary.to_string())
print()

# Occupancy distribution with anomaly zones
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
for snap in sorted(df_occ['snapshot_date'].unique()):
    vals = df_occ.loc[df_occ['snapshot_date'] == snap, 'occ_90'].dropna()
    ax.hist(vals, bins=50, alpha=0.4, label=snap, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)

ax.axvspan(0.95, 1.01, color='red', alpha=0.12, label='Saturated zone (>=0.95)')
ax.axvspan(-0.01, 0.005, color='blue', alpha=0.12, label='Zero zone (==0)')
ax.set_xlabel('Occupancy rate (90-day window)')
ax.set_ylabel('Number of listings')
ax.set_title('Occupancy distribution by snapshot\n'
             'Shaded zones = anomaly flags')
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()

8b Refining occupancy flags: hotels and new listings
Not all extremes are anomalies:

Saturated (occ >= 0.95) could be hotels or professional hospitality properties that legitimately run near capacity.
Zero occupancy could be brand-new listings that haven’t launched yet (no first review = never booked).

Cross-reference with property_type, room_type, and first_review_date from listings_property_cleaned to separate legitimate cases from true anomalies, then update the flag definitions.


Show code
# --- 8b: Break down saturated & zero-occ by property type and listing age ---
sql_enrich = f"""
SELECT
    m.snapshot_date::text AS snapshot_date,
    m.listing_id,
    m.occ_90,
    m.days_90,
    p.property_type,
    p.room_type,
    p.first_review_date
FROM {METRICS_TABLE} m
JOIN {TABLE} p
    ON p.snapshot_date = m.snapshot_date AND p.listing_id = m.listing_id
WHERE m.days_90 > 0
"""
df_enrich = pd.read_sql(sql_enrich, engine)

# Classify property types as hotel-like
hotel_keywords = ['hotel', 'hostel', 'motel', 'resort', 'apart-hotel', 'aparthotel',
                  'boutique hotel', 'bed and breakfast']
df_enrich['is_hotel_like'] = (
    df_enrich['property_type'].str.contains('|'.join(hotel_keywords), case=False, na=False) |
    df_enrich['room_type'].str.contains('hotel', case=False, na=False)
)

# Classify new listings (no first_review = never booked)
df_enrich['is_new_listing'] = df_enrich['first_review_date'].isna()

# --- Saturated breakdown ---
saturated = df_enrich[df_enrich['occ_90'] >= 0.95]
sat_breakdown = (
    saturated.groupby('snapshot_date')
    .agg(
        total_saturated=('listing_id', 'count'),
        hotel_like=('is_hotel_like', 'sum'),
        non_hotel=('is_hotel_like', lambda s: (~s).sum()),
    )
    .assign(
        pct_hotel=lambda d: round(100 * d.hotel_like / d.total_saturated, 1),
    )
)
print('=== Saturated occupancy (>= 0.95) breakdown ===')
print(sat_breakdown.to_string())
print()

# Top property_types among saturated
sat_types = (
    saturated.groupby('property_type')['listing_id'].count()
    .sort_values(ascending=False).head(15)
)
print('Top property_types among saturated-occupancy listings:')
for pt, cnt in sat_types.items():
    hotel_tag = ' ← hotel-like' if any(kw in str(pt).lower() for kw in hotel_keywords) else ''
    print(f"  {pt:40s} {cnt:>5,}{hotel_tag}")

print()

# --- Zero-occ breakdown ---
zero_occ = df_enrich[(df_enrich['occ_90'] == 0) | (df_enrich['occ_90'].isna() & (df_enrich['days_90'] > 0))]
zero_breakdown = (
    zero_occ.groupby('snapshot_date')
    .agg(
        total_zero=('listing_id', 'count'),
        new_listing=('is_new_listing', 'sum'),
        established=('is_new_listing', lambda s: (~s).sum()),
    )
    .assign(
        pct_new=lambda d: round(100 * d.new_listing / d.total_zero, 1),
    )
)
print('=== Zero occupancy breakdown ===')
print(zero_breakdown.to_string())
print()

# Visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

# Left: saturated — hotel vs non-hotel

title: Pricing Consistency & Data Quality Analysis
text:
9 Data gap analysis
Three dimensions of data completeness:

9a Calendar coverage: Ratio of actual calendar rows to 365 expected days. Listings below 80 % coverage are flagged — metrics built on sparse data are unreliable.
9b Missing price on booked days: Booked (available = 0) but price IS NULL. ADR / RevPAR are understated when booked-day prices are missing.
9c Listing churn: Listings that appear or disappear across snapshots. Churn complicates longitudinal analysis and imputation.



Show code
# --- 9a: Calendar coverage per listing per snapshot ---
sql_cov = f"""
SELECT
    snapshot_date::text AS snapshot_date,
    listing_id,
    host_id,
    COUNT(*) AS cal_rows,
    ROUND(COUNT(*)::numeric / 365, 3) AS coverage
FROM {CAL_TABLE}
GROUP BY snapshot_date, listing_id, host_id
"""
df_cov = pd.read_sql(sql_cov, engine)
df_cov['low_coverage'] = df_cov['coverage'] < 0.80

cov_summary = (
    df_cov.groupby('snapshot_date')
    .agg(
        listings=('listing_id', 'count'),
        median_coverage=('coverage', 'median'),
        low_cov_count=('low_coverage', 'sum'),
    )
    .assign(pct_low_cov=lambda d: round(100 * d.low_cov_count / d.listings, 1))
)
print('=== Calendar coverage (rows / 365 expected) ===')
print(cov_summary.to_string())
print()

# --- 9b: Missing price on booked days ---
sql_price_gap = f"""
SELECT
    snapshot_date::text AS snapshot_date,
    listing_id,
    host_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN available = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS booked_days,
    SUM(CASE WHEN available = 0 AND price IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS booked_no_price
FROM {CAL_TABLE}
GROUP BY snapshot_date, listing_id, host_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN available = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
"""
df_pgap = pd.read_sql(sql_price_gap, engine)
df_pgap['pct_missing'] = round(100 * df_pgap['booked_no_price'] / df_pgap['booked_days'], 1)

title: Pricing Consistency & Data Quality Analysis
text:
10 Combined quality flags → airbnb_features.listing_quality_flags
Materialise a single boolean-flag table combining all anomaly detections above. One row per (snapshot_date, listing_id). Downstream consumers can filter or weight listings by flag status.








Flag
Source
Threshold




flag_adr_outlier
§7a IQR
ADR outside Q1−1.5×IQR … Q3+1.5×IQR


flag_adr_spike
§7b temporal
|Δ ADR %| > 50 % vs. previous snapshot


flag_occ_saturated
§8 + §8b
occ_90 >= 0.95 AND NOT hotel-like property


flag_occ_zero
§8 + §8b
occ_90 == 0 with data present AND has first_review (not brand-new)


flag_low_coverage
§9a
calendar rows / 365 < 0.80





Show code
sql_flags = f"""
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS airbnb_features;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS airbnb_features.listing_quality_flags;

CREATE TABLE airbnb_features.listing_quality_flags AS
WITH
-- Base population: all listing-snapshots from metrics
base AS (
    SELECT snapshot_date, listing_id, host_id,
           adr_90, occ_90, days_90
    FROM {METRICS_TABLE}
),
-- Property attributes for occupancy flag refinement
prop AS (
    SELECT snapshot_date, listing_id,
           property_type, room_type, first_review_date
    FROM {TABLE}
),
-- 7a: IQR-based ADR outliers
iqr_stats AS (
    SELECT snapshot_date,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY adr_90) AS q1,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY adr_90) AS q3
    FROM {METRICS_TABLE}
    WHERE adr_90 IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY snapshot_date
),
adr_outliers AS (
    SELECT m.snapshot_date, m.listing_id,
           (m.adr_90 < s.q1 - 1.5 * (s.q3 - s.q1)
            OR m.adr_90 > s.q3 + 1.5 * (s.q3 - s.q1)) AS flag_adr_outlier
    FROM {METRICS_TABLE} m
    JOIN iqr_stats s USING (snapshot_date)
    WHERE m.adr_90 IS NOT NULL
),
-- 7b: Temporal ADR spikes
adr_changes AS (
    SELECT snapshot_date, listing_id,
           adr_90,
           LAG(adr_90) OVER (PARTITION BY listing_id ORDER BY snapshot_date) AS prev_adr
    FROM {METRICS_TABLE}
    WHERE adr_90 IS NOT NULL
),
adr_spikes AS (
    SELECT snapshot_date, listing_id,
           (ABS(adr_90 - prev_adr) / NULLIF(prev_adr, 0) > 0.50) AS flag_adr_spike
    FROM adr_changes
    WHERE prev_adr IS NOT NULL
),
-- 9a: Calendar coverage
cal_coverage AS (
    SELECT snapshot_date, listing_id,
           COUNT(*)::numeric / 365 AS coverage
    FROM {CAL_TABLE}
    GROUP BY snapshot_date, listing_id
)
SELECT
    b.snapshot_date,
    b.listing_id,
    b.host_id,
    COALESCE(ao.flag_adr_outlier, false)                       AS flag_adr_outlier,
    COALESCE(asp.flag_adr_spike, false)                        AS flag_adr_spike,
    -- Saturated: occ >= 0.95 AND NOT hotel-like property
    (b.occ_90 IS NOT NULL AND b.occ_90 >= 0.95
     AND NOT (
         COALESCE(p.property_type, '') ~* '(hotel|hostel|motel|resort|apart-hotel|aparthotel|bed and breakfast)'
         OR COALESCE(p.room_type, '') ~* 'hotel'
     ))                                                        AS flag_occ_saturated,
    -- Zero: occ == 0 AND has first_review (not brand-new unlaunched listing)
    (b.days_90 > 0 AND COALESCE(b.occ_90, 0) = 0
     AND p.first_review_date IS NOT NULL)                      AS flag_occ_zero,
    COALESCE(cc.coverage < 0.80, false)                        AS flag_low_coverage
FROM base b
LEFT JOIN prop         p   ON p.snapshot_date  = b.snapshot_date
                           AND p.listing_id    = b.listing_id
LEFT JOIN adr_outliers ao  ON ao.snapshot_date = b.snapshot_date
                           AND ao.listing_id   = b.listing_id
LEFT JOIN adr_spikes   asp ON asp.snapshot_date = b.snapshot_date
                           AND asp.listing_id   = b.listing_id
LEFT JOIN cal_coverage cc  ON cc.snapshot_date  = b.snapshot_date
                           AND cc.listing_id    = b.listing_id;

ALTER TABLE airbnb_features.listing_quality_flags
    ADD PRIMARY KEY (snapshot_date, listing_id);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_quality_flags_host
    ON airbnb_features.listing_quality_flags (host_id);

ANALYZE airbnb_features.listing_quality_flags;
"""

with engine.begin() as conn:
    conn.execute(text(sql_flags))

print("airbnb_features.listing_quality_flags written successfully (refined flags).")

# --- Verification & summary ---
df_flags = pd.read_sql("""
    SELECT
        snapshot_date::text,
        COUNT(*) AS listings,
        SUM(flag_adr_outlier::int)    AS adr_outlier,
        SUM(flag_adr_spike::int)      AS adr_spike,
        SUM(flag_occ_saturated::int)  AS occ_saturated,
        SUM(flag_occ_zero::int)       AS occ_zero,
        SUM(flag_low_coverage::int)   AS low_coverage,
        SUM(CASE WHEN flag_adr_outlier OR flag_adr_spike OR flag_occ_saturated
                      OR flag_occ_zero OR flag_low_coverage
                 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)   AS any_flag
    FROM airbnb_features.listing_quality_flags
    GROUP BY snapshot_date
    ORDER BY snapshot_date
""", engine)
print()
print(df_flags.to_string(index=False))

# Stacked bar: flag prevalence per snapshot
flag_cols = ['adr_outlier', 'adr_spike', 'occ_saturated',
             'occ_zero', 'low_coverage']
flag_colors = ['#e41a1c', '#ff7f00', '#984ea3', '#377eb8', '#4daf4a']

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
x = np.arange(len(df_flags))
bottom = np.zeros(len(df_flags))
for col, clr in zip(flag_cols, flag_colors):
    vals = df_flags[col].values.astype(float)
    ax.bar(x, vals, bottom=bottom, label=col, color=clr, alpha=0.85)
    bottom += vals

ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(df_flags['snapshot_date'], rotation=25, ha='right')
ax.set_ylabel('Flagged listings')
ax.set_title('Quality flag prevalence by snapshot (refined)\n'
             'Hotels excluded from occ_saturated; new listings excluded from occ_zero')
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

text:
11 Impact analysis: all listings vs. clean (unflagged) subset
Join metrics with listing_quality_flags and compare key distributional statistics — ADR, occupancy, RevPAR — across cohorts. Restricted to the 4 early snapshots (2024-06-26 … 2025-03-19) where ADR is actual, not carry-forward.



Cohort
Definition




All
Every listing-snapshot with actual ADR


Clean
Rows where no quality flag is TRUE


Flagged
Rows with at least one flag



If the flags are catching real noise, we expect the clean subset to have tighter distributions (lower std, narrower IQR) and potentially different central tendency (lower mean ADR if luxury outliers removed; higher mean occupancy if zero-occ listings removed).


Show code
FLAGS_TABLE = 'airbnb_features.listing_quality_flags'

# Pull actual metrics + flags (early snapshots only — no imputation involved)
sql_compare = f"""
SELECT
    m.snapshot_date::text AS snapshot_date,
    m.listing_id,
    m.adr_90  AS adr,
    m.occ_90,
    m.revpar_90,
    COALESCE(f.flag_adr_outlier,   false) AS flag_adr_outlier,
    COALESCE(f.flag_adr_spike,     false) AS flag_adr_spike,
    COALESCE(f.flag_occ_saturated, false) AS flag_occ_saturated,
    COALESCE(f.flag_occ_zero,      false) AS flag_occ_zero,
    COALESCE(f.flag_low_coverage,  false) AS flag_low_coverage
FROM {METRICS_TABLE} m
LEFT JOIN {FLAGS_TABLE} f
    ON f.snapshot_date = m.snapshot_date AND f.listing_id = m.listing_id
WHERE m.adr_90 IS NOT NULL
"""
df = pd.read_sql(sql_compare, engine)

df['any_flag'] = (
    df['flag_adr_outlier'] | df['flag_adr_spike'] |
    df['flag_occ_saturated'] | df['flag_occ_zero'] |
    df['flag_low_coverage']
)
df['cohort'] = np.where(df['any_flag'], 'flagged', 'clean')

# --- Per-snapshot summary stats: All vs Clean vs Flagged ---
def cohort_stats(group):
    return pd.Series({
        'n':          len(group),
        'mean_adr':   round(group['adr'].mean(), 2),
        'median_adr': round(group['adr'].median(), 2),
        'std_adr':    round(group['adr'].std(), 2),
        'p25_adr':    round(group['adr'].quantile(0.25), 2),
        'p75_adr':    round(group['adr'].quantile(0.75), 2),
        'mean_occ':   round(group['occ_90'].mean(), 3) if group['occ_90'].notna().any() else None,
        'median_occ': round(group['occ_90'].median(), 3) if group['occ_90'].notna().any() else None,
        'mean_revpar':   round(group['revpar_90'].mean(), 2) if group['revpar_90'].notna().any() else None,
        'median_revpar': round(group['revpar_90'].median(), 2) if group['revpar_90'].notna().any() else None,
    })

stats_all     = df.groupby('snapshot_date').apply(cohort_stats, include_groups=False).reset_index()
stats_all.insert(1, 'cohort', 'all')
stats_clean   = df[~df['any_flag']].groupby('snapshot_date').apply(cohort_stats, include_groups=False).reset_index()
stats_clean.insert(1, 'cohort', 'clean')
stats_flagged = df[df['any_flag']].groupby('snapshot_date').apply(cohort_stats, include_groups=False).reset_index()
stats_flagged.insert(1, 'cohort', 'flagged')

df_stats = pd.concat([stats_all, stats_clean, stats_flagged], ignore_index=True)
df_stats = df_stats.sort_values(['snapshot_date', 'cohort']).reset_index(drop=True)

print('=== Distributional comparison: All vs Clean vs Flagged ===')
print(df_stats.to_string(index=False))

# --- Bar charts: cohort counts + key metrics per snapshot ---
snaps = sorted(df_stats['snapshot_date'].unique())
x = np.arange(len(snaps))
width = 0.25
cohorts = ['all', 'clean', 'flagged']
cohort_colors = {'all': '#4C72B0', 'clean': '#55A868', 'flagged': '#e41a1c'}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(15, 10))

chart_cfg = [
    ('n',          'Listing count',         axes[0, 0]),
    ('median_adr', 'Median ADR ($/night)',   axes[0, 1]),
    ('median_occ', 'Median Occupancy (90d)', axes[1, 0]),
    ('std_adr',    'Std ADR ($/night)',      axes[1, 1]),
]

for metric, ylabel, ax in chart_cfg:
    for i, cohort in enumerate(cohorts):
        vals = df_stats.loc[df_stats['cohort'] == cohort].set_index('snapshot_date').reindex(snaps)[metric].values
        bars = ax.bar(x + (i - 1) * width, vals.astype(float), width,
                      label=cohort.capitalize(), color=cohort_colors[cohort], alpha=0.85)
        # annotate bars
        for xi, v in enumerate(vals):
            if not np.isnan(float(v)):
                fmt = f'{int(v):,}' if metric == 'n' else (f'{float(v):.2f}' if metric == 'median_occ' else f'${float(v):,.0f}')
                ax.text(xi + (i - 1) * width, float(v), fmt,
                        ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=7, rotation=0)

    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(snaps, rotation=25, ha='right', fontsize=8)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    ax.set_title(ylabel)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)

fig.suptitle('All vs Clean vs Flagged — early snapshots (actual ADR)', fontsize=12)
fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.95))
plt.show()

early_snaps = sorted(df['snapshot_date'].unique())

11b Flag-by-flag isolation
The all-or-nothing view above removes ~30 % of listings at once. Which individual flag is doing the heavy lifting? For each flag we exclude only listings carrying that single flag and measure the % shift in mean ADR, std ADR, mean occupancy, and median RevPAR vs. the full set.
This tells us whether the −40 % mean-ADR swing is driven primarily by adr_outlier (luxury tail), occ_zero (inactive listings with weird ADR), or some combination.


Show code
# --- Flag-by-flag isolation: exclude ONE flag at a time ---
flag_names = ['flag_adr_outlier', 'flag_adr_spike', 'flag_occ_saturated',
              'flag_occ_zero', 'flag_low_coverage']
flag_labels = ['ADR outlier', 'ADR spike', 'Occ saturated',
               'Occ zero', 'Low coverage']

# Restrict to early snapshots where flags are meaningful
df_early = df.copy()

metrics_keys = ['mean_adr', 'std_adr', 'mean_occ', 'median_revpar']

def calc_metrics(sub):
    return {
        'mean_adr':      sub['adr'].mean(),
        'std_adr':       sub['adr'].std(),
        'mean_occ':      sub['occ_90'].mean() if sub['occ_90'].notna().any() else np.nan,
        'median_revpar': sub['revpar_90'].median() if sub['revpar_90'].notna().any() else np.nan,
    }

rows = []
for snap in sorted(df_early['snapshot_date'].unique()):
    sub_all = df_early[df_early['snapshot_date'] == snap]
    base = calc_metrics(sub_all)

    for flag_col, flag_lbl in zip(flag_names, flag_labels):
        excluded = sub_all[flag_col].sum()
        sub_excl = sub_all[~sub_all[flag_col]]
        excl_m = calc_metrics(sub_excl)

        row = {
            'snapshot': snap,
            'excluded_flag': flag_lbl,
            'n_excluded': int(excluded),
            'pct_excluded': round(100 * excluded / len(sub_all), 1),
        }
        for mk in metrics_keys:
            if base[mk] and base[mk] != 0 and not np.isnan(base[mk]):
                row[f'{mk}_pct_chg'] = round(100 * (excl_m[mk] - base[mk]) / abs(base[mk]), 2)
            else:
                row[f'{mk}_pct_chg'] = np.nan
        rows.append(row)

df_iso = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print('=== Flag-by-flag impact (early snapshots, each flag excluded independently) ===')
print(df_iso.to_string(index=False))

title: The Best and Worst Bets in the Broward Airbnb Market
text:
Should you invest in a Broward County Airbnb? And if so, where?
South Florida’s short-term rental market is booming — or so the Instagram ads would have you believe. The reality is more nuanced. Broward County (Fort Lauderdale and surrounding cities) has 17,000+ active Airbnb listings, and nearly half of them are controlled by corporate operators running portfolios of 10, 50, or even 2,700 properties.
If you’re an individual investor thinking about buying a condo or house to list on Airbnb, you need to understand what you’re walking into. This analysis uses 4 quarterly snapshots (June 2024, September 2024, December 2024, March 2025) from Inside Airbnb to answer the questions that matter:

How much can you realistically earn?
Which neighborhoods are worth targeting?
What kind of property should you buy?
Can you actually compete with the big operators?

Spoiler: The answer is yes — but only if you’re strategic about it.

section: 1. The Market Landscape: Who Owns Broward’s Airbnb Supply?
text:
1. The Market Landscape: Who Owns Broward’s Airbnb Supply?
Before you invest a dollar, you need to understand the competitive landscape. The Broward Airbnb market isn’t just mom-and-pop hosts renting out spare bedrooms. Nearly 43% of active listings are controlled by corporate operators — companies running 10+ properties, or well-known management brands like Stay Sol, Evolve, and Vacasa.
But here’s the thing that should give you hope: corporate doesn’t mean better.


Show code
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Identify corporate hosts
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
corp_keywords = ["stay sol", "evolve", "vacasa", "sonder", "blueground", "kasa",
                 "live suite", "roompicks", "golden stays", "stay today",
                 "latitude key", "stay hospitality", "newman hospitality",
                 "regal hospitality", "coastal hospitality"]

named_corp_ids = set()
for kw in corp_keywords:
    ids = lst[lst["host_name"].str.lower().str.contains(kw, na=False)]["host_id"].unique()
    named_corp_ids.update(ids)

big_hosts = lst.groupby("host_id")["id"].nunique()
commercial_ids = set(big_hosts[big_hosts >= 10].index) | named_corp_ids

# Tag in adv
adv["is_corporate"] = adv["host_id"].isin(commercial_ids)

# Build market segments for pie chart
# Corporate
n_corp = adv[adv["is_corporate"]].shape[0]
# Inactive / near-zero occupancy (non-corporate)
n_inactive = adv[(~adv["is_corporate"]) & (adv["occupancy_avg"] <= 0)].shape[0]
# Hotel rooms / shared rooms (non-corporate, active)
n_hotel = adv[(~adv["is_corporate"]) & (adv["occupancy_avg"] > 0) &
              (~adv["room_type"].isin(["Entire home/apt", "Private room"]))].shape[0]
# Luxury / high ADR (non-corporate, active, right room type, ADR > $500)
n_luxury = adv[(~adv["is_corporate"]) & (adv["occupancy_avg"] > 0) &
               (adv["room_type"].isin(["Entire home/apt", "Private room"])) &
               (adv["adr_avg"] > 500)].shape[0]
# Mom-and-pop
n_mp = adv[(~adv["is_corporate"]) & (adv["occupancy_avg"] > 0) &
           (adv["room_type"].isin(["Entire home/apt", "Private room"])) &
           (adv["adr_avg"] > 0) & (adv["adr_avg"] <= 500)].shape[0]

print(f"Mom-and-pop:    {n_mp:,} ({n_mp/total:.0%})")

2. Know Your Competition: The Corporate Operators

What’s going on with Stay Sol? They control 2,700+ listings with a $1,000 median ADR but only 8% occupancy, yielding just $47 RevPAR. A few hypotheses:

Monthly rental pricing baked into nightly rates — many of these may be long-term furnished rentals listed on Airbnb as a marketing channel, with the calendar showing as “available” even when occupied on a monthly lease.
New listings still ramping up — a portfolio that size may have a large share of recently added properties that haven’t gained traction yet.
Intentional luxury positioning — pricing high and accepting low occupancy to maintain brand perception, making it up on the occasional week-long booking.

Evolve is the standout. At $148 RevPAR, they’re meaningfully outperforming both the mom-and-pop median and every other corporate operator. They achieve this through a balanced approach: premium rates ($586 ADR) paired with 20% occupancy — not spectacular, but far better than their peers.
Vacasa is essentially inactive in this market — 1% occupancy on 292 listings suggests they may be winding down their Broward presence or transitioning properties.
The bottom line for individual investors: most corporate operators are not your competition. Their occupancy rates are terrible. The competition that matters is other mom-and-pop hosts doing the same thing you plan to do.

title: The Best and Worst Bets in the Broward Airbnb Market
text:
3. Filtering to Your Universe
To make this analysis useful, we need to compare apples to apples. A mom-and-pop investor isn’t buying a shared room in a hostel or pricing at $2,000/night. We need to filter down to your actual competitive universe.
The mom-and-pop filter:

Entire home/apt or Private room (not shared rooms or hotel rooms)
ADR between $1 and $500/night (excludes luxury and mispriced listings)
Host with fewer than 10 listings (not a commercial operator)
Not a named corporate brand (Stay Sol, Evolve, Vacasa, etc.)
Occupancy > 0 (actually attempting to rent)



Show code
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Apply mom-and-pop filter
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
mp_mask = (
    adv["room_type"].isin(["Entire home/apt", "Private room"]) &
    (adv["adr_avg"] > 0) & (adv["adr_avg"] <= 500) &
    (~adv["host_id"].isin(commercial_ids)) &
    (adv["occupancy_avg"] > 0)
)
mp = adv[mp_mask].copy()

print(f"Total listings in dataset:       {adv.shape[0]:,}")
print(f"After mom-and-pop filter:        {mp.shape[0]:,}")
print(f"Removed:                         {adv.shape[0] - mp.shape[0]:,}")
print()
print("What was excluded:")
print(f"  Corporate operators (10+ or named): {adv['is_corporate'].sum():,}")
print(f"  Zero occupancy (inactive):          {(adv['occupancy_avg'] <= 0).sum():,}")
